todays_goal: Write from evidence to inference rather than retelling plot.

lessons.subject: writing
lessons.previous_learning: Day 17 analytical paragraph was complete and organized; evidence chains can still become more exact.
lessons.course_context: Connect the inference review directly to analytical writing.
learning_objectives: Explain why each clue supports a character claim.
lessons.why_it_matters: Analytical writing turns evidence into explanation.

vocabulary.definition: why the clue supports the claim

lessons.written_instruction: Atticus: use EVIDENCE -> INFERENCE -> REASONING. Do not stop after telling what happened.

worked_examples.title: Amara
worked_examples.problem: Amara walks toward the buses even though her bus is elsewhere.
worked_examples.explanation: The choice costs her time, so the help is deliberate.

independent_practice.prompt: Write 6-8 sentences: What does Amara's choice show about her character? Use two clues and explain what each tells you.

exit_ticket.answer: Claim, two clues, explanation after each, no plot-only retelling, conclusion.

lessons.voice_prompt: Do not dictate. Ask: What is your claim? What clue proves it? What does that clue tell you? Why does it matter? If he only retells, ask what the detail shows.
